question.text: A Category III AIF subscribed to Pre-IPO shares of a company. Under which regulation is a lock-in period imposed on these shares from the date of listing?

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 10.1.4.3 explicitly cites SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018 as the source of the Pre-IPO lock-in rule for institutional investors (including AIFs) subscribing to Pre-IPO or QIP shares. The Trap: Option B regulates AIFs themselves but not the ICDR lock-in. Option C governs listing disclosures, not issue. Option D is relevant to issue of shares but not lock-in. Cross-Exam Context: XV (Research Analyst) and XIX-C cover ICDR. III-A/C (Compliance) tests ICDR interplay with AIF Regs. Manager's Pro-Tip: Flag Pre-IPO positions in the PMS with lock-in expiry dates; marking-to-market during lock-in needs an illiquidity discount (typically 10-15%). Release the discount in a straight-line over the lock-in period to smooth NAV jumps.
